In summary, our research is concerned with
the creation and analysis of large-scale, complex, multi-media collections of primary and secondary sources.
the development of new methods for the representation, organization, and analysis of large collections of texts and images.
the design of a digital library collection that is not only a useful resource for scholars, but is also designed to support new forms of scholarship and new forms of interaction with the material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a digital library of this kind is a very useful research tool for scholars of all kinds.
we are now able to use the London collection to answer questions that were previously impossible, and to do so with greater speed and accuracy than was possible with the earlier collections.
the London collection is a model of a humanities digital library, but it is only a model, not a final solution to the problems of humanities computing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a large, rich, and flexible digital collection that can serve as a model for future digital library collections in the humanities.
the London collection has been used by scholars and students to answer questions about the city of London in ways that are not possible with traditional library materials.

we have built a digital library of the London past that can be used for research in the humanities, but that we have also built an infrastructure that allows us to create digital libraries for other collections in the humanities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the most effective way to build a humanities digital library is not to encode every word in every document, but rather to encode the most important words, and to link them to the most important words in other documents.
the humanities can be best served by digital libraries that are not primarily based on full-text searching, but rather on richly linked and structured collections of documents and images.
a humanities digital library should not be designed as a hypertext but as a data set that can be manipulated by users in a variety of different ways.
